name: Teach the World Foundation
mission: To revolutionize education for underserved communities around the globe by pioneering innovative solutions to enhance literacy and learning through digital technology.
theoryOfChange: Teach the World Foundation has uploaded a document titled "61951_TTW Theory of Change.pdf" to their profile on the MIT Solve platform, explicitly indicating a published Theory of Change. Additionally, their GlobalGiving profile details "THE TEACH THE WORLD FOUNDATION LEARNING MODEL," which outlines their mission to use digital, game-based learning technologies to address illiteracy, access to education, and teacher shortages in the developing world. This model describes the implementation by facilitators and the rigorous testing of learning technologies to achieve significant learning gains. The organization's website also describes their approach to providing quality education through MicroSchools, digitizing existing traditional classrooms, and implementing smartphone-based learning programs.

rich_narrative.summary: Teach-the-World Foundation (TTWF) is a digital-first educational non-profit that aims to solve global illiteracy through scalable learning models. <cite id="1">founded in 2015</cite>, the organization focuses on deploying digital tools in low-income areas to help children learn to read and write. Their model includes <cite id="3">Microschools, InSchool programs, and AtHome learning</cite> initiatives. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="1">total revenue of $363,707</cite>, maintaining a steady financial position despite a <cite id="1">slight three-year revenue decline of 2.1%</cite>. The foundation operates primarily in <cite id="3">Pakistan, Malawi, and Bangladesh</cite>, leveraging technology to bypass traditional infrastructure barriers. While the organization is relatively small, it has achieved <cite id="9">an overall score of 84.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting a balance between program delivery and administrative oversight. The foundation's approach is characterized by <cite id="3">digital literacy and confidence building</cite> among students who previously lacked access to quality educational resources.
